title: GOE bulk universality for fixed-degree random regular graphs
main_claim: For every fixed d>=3 and fixed E in the open Kesten-McKay bulk, the unfolded eigenvalue point process of a uniform simple d-regular graph at E converges (Laplace functionals) to the GOE bulk sine_1 process along all admissible n. This resolves Bourgade-Huang Conjecture 2.11.

issues.description: The bound on the cell-frequency variance of Q keeps only the off-diagonal (distinct-edge) covariance term C/(sqrt n eta^2). It drops the diagonal 1/(nd) term and the dependence between pairs of edges that share an endpoint. Both are of lower order, so the stated n^{4l gamma - 1/4 + alpha} rate is unaffected. This is terseness, not a gap.
issues.evidence: "Consequently each cell frequency of Q has variance O(n^{-1/2}eta^{-2})."

issues.description: The off-block entries of M_{n,k}(z_0) are shown to be O(S^{-c}) only in an averaged/Markov sense over random edge samples. This is enough because the edges are sampled at random and the statement is probabilistic, but the passage is compressed.
issues.evidence: "Markov's inequality makes their resolvent entries O(S^{-c}), after decreasing c."

coverage: I read every section in full (main.tex and sections 01-06). Checks I ran: (1) the tree log-potential identity -U(E) = -1/2 log d + (d-1)/2 log a - d/4 log(1-p^2), numerically with mpmath for d=3,4,7 and several E: it matches. (2) The Jacobian and determinant constants in the projected-entropy lemma, recomputed by hand: they cancel exactly against the global entropy. (3) The tree covariance mapping to Id_D (1-g=a). (4) The weighted frame identity (eq:ent-frame), numerically. (5) The tensor-coercivity Lemma ent:tensor, numerically on the swap-constrained symmetric tensor space for (d,E,j) = (3,0,3/4/5), (3,2.7,3), (4,1,3), (4,3.4,4) and l=2: the minimum eigenvalue is strictly positive. I also checked the equality-case commutator argument by hand. (6) The Hermite/relative-entropy expansion and the choice of tau in the Gaussian criterion. (7) The two-edge switch algebra: F B F^T equals the adjacency change, (I+UB)Uhat=U, and the off-diagonal entry gives q^2-q-m^2=0, whose discriminant (E^2-4(d-1))/d^2 < 0 in the bulk. (8) The T_O group-action identity B_{OO'} = B_O + D_O B_{O'} D_O^T, plus R_U invariance via [J, diag(U,U)]=0 and generation of O(k) by reflections. (9) The Woodbury reduction to D + G beta G^T, and the s_1, s_2 bounds (Tr(C_k B) = 2p Tr(O-I) = O(r theta^2)). (10) The weighted Bernstein bounds, the Schur-complement exponent bookkeeping (6tau - chi/100, etc.), the inner-resolvent bound at height h=T^2, and the Lindeberg exponent -0.44 + 1.5tau. (11) The DBM inputs: regularity down to u ~ T^{1/2} = K^{50tau} is supplied by the mesoscopic law (any delta>0), and the time window t*/(g m^tau) = m^{49tau} and t*/(m^{-tau}G^2) -> 0 both hold, as do the free-convolution density fix and the unfolding coordinates. (12) The Forrester-Rains decimation count bound and the Bonferroni bracketing. I did not independently check the cited external inputs: the exact hypotheses of Huang-Yau's theorems and of Landon-Sosoe-Yau Theorem 2.2 were taken as quoted.
